newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Mobile phones blamed for missing racing pigeons.
newsitem.headline: Mobile phones blamed for missing racing pigeons.

text.p: Ireland's pigeon-racing fraternity have their feathers ruffled. Their birds are going missing, and they suspect mobile phones may be disrupting their homing instincts.

"Pigeons navigate through using the sun and the magnetic fields of the earth. There may be a problem with mobile phones, there's so much equipment going through the air now," Tony Kehoe, president of one pigeon-racing club told the Irish Times.
Membership has fallen drastically over recent years because so many birds have gone missing.
Jim Power, the club secretary, told the newspaper that predatory falcons might account for some of the losses, but speculated that mobile phones must also be to blame..
Spokesmen for Ireland's two main mobile phone operators, Eircell and Esat Digifone, suggested that perhaps the birds had just gone somewhere warmer than Ireland.
